Marianas participants in WIC, the nutrition program for Women, Infants, and Children, will be allowed to exchange recalled infant formula under a waiver issued by the .@USDA.

Read more:
https://t.co/GmxZ7KHL79 https://t.co/hIDnag5AIj

The FY22 spending bill also raises funding for the Commonwealth’s Nutrition Assistance Program, NAP to $30 million.

Read more:
https://t.co/3kpU3KPib2 https://t.co/3avBRUcK40

The Marianas Nutrition Assistance Program would get another bump in funding to $30.7 million in the FY23 budget that Pres. Biden sent to Congress last Monday.

For more highlights including more money for schools, college students and sewer infrastructure:
https://t.co/KVrTTMHmiU https://t.co/YVYmdpkpER

The House Appropriations Agriculture Subcommittee added four of my requests for Marianas community projects—worth $6,214,941—to its FY23 spending bill.

Read more about the funding for our libraries, renal treatment on Tinian & CHCC parking:
https://t.co/xs8guhgAHi https://t.co/CC9gS2DRKg

The Appropriations Committee approved $30.7 million for the Marianas Nutrition Assistance Program in the FY 2023 spending bill for .@USDA.

Read more:
 https://t.co/FhLzJUZw4a https://t.co/Fj7s9njg47

TriWest Vice President for Pacific Operations Karl Kiyokawa & Chief Administrative Officer Jim Griffith briefed me on the workplan for their first visit to the Marianas since the pandemic began.

TriWest coordinates payments to veterans' health care providers. https://t.co/RZiojt0pIN

Participants in the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) will gain access to a wider variety of nutritious foods and have more flexibility for special dietary needs, .@USDA FNS announced Friday.

Read more:
https://t.co/EzzoT8b5Lt https://t.co/8ndoe5lUc6

.@USDA Rural Dev. awarded more than $1.3 million to .@cnmichcc to help improve its medical operations & patient care. 

$953k will be used to renovate & upgrade all 86 patient rooms at the Saipan hospital, w/ 16 of the rooms to be converted to airborne infection isolation rooms. https://t.co/fgw4z1S7o7

.@DeptVetAffairs announced that veterans in acute suicidal crisis will now be able to go to any VA or non-VA healthcare facility for emergency healthcare at no cost.

Read more:
https://t.co/s9RhM2isWl https://t.co/dbI93YBv7a

Veterans in the Marianas would have their own Vet Center & a Community Based Outpatient Clinic run by .@DeptVetAffairs under the Vet CENTERS for Mental Health Act (H.R. 733) that Rep. Mikie Sherrill &I re-introduced Wednesday.

Read more:
https://t.co/IXxfXtQc93 https://t.co/o5ZVKWwSA2

Though federal Medicaid funding for the NMI  now increases annually at the rate that health care costs rise, it's still limited to that fixed amount.

To cont. my work to give people in the NMI similar levels of fed. support I re-intro'd the Insular Area Medicaid Parity Act. https://t.co/N70fgVXtKD

Your congressional office was informed this month that veterans who are eligible for beneficiary travel will no longer have to pay out-of-pocket for air travel & lodging to their VA-approved appointments. 

For more info: https://t.co/vwbss6xyW0 https://t.co/1hsg9pahyT

Veterans & service members enrolled in Veterans’ Group Life Insurance & Servicemembers Group Life Insurance will see their max amount of life insurance coverage increase from $400K to $500K, according to an announcement from .@DeptVetAffairs.

More info:
https://t.co/ybkadsnnIp https://t.co/6o05ahH94p

Low-income households and recipients of federal assistance programs like Medicaid, WIC, the Pell Grant, & veterans’ pension & survivors’ benefits may qualify for a discount on new or current internet service & discounts on digital devices.

More info:
https://t.co/bMsh8PWJuW https://t.co/tlQPSI3IMy

The Marianas Medicaid program would get more funds under legislation I introduced Thursday. The Northern Mariana Islands Medicaid Equivalence Act provides a Medicaid grant to the Marianas that matches that of Am. Samoa—a territory w/ virtually the same population & income levels. https://t.co/S2c1BxF4IY

During stressful times like a typhoon, feelings of anxiousness or even PTSD-related triggers may arise.

If you need someone to talk to, dial "988."

988 is the free, 24/7 number for those experiencing a mental health or substance-related crisis. https://t.co/fNDR4cbr8M

Your congressional office has received calls re: denied applications for Medicare Part D, having to do w/ them recognizing NMI PO Box addresses, . If any issues now or in the future, reach out to me at kilili@mail.house.gov or contact your local office in Rota, Tinian or Saipan. https://t.co/Ii7xrNPSPS

Your congressional office has rec'd calls re: denied applications for Medicare Part D, due to not recognizing NMI PO Box addresses. 

If any issues now or in the future, reach out to me at kilili@mail.house.gov or call your local office. https://t.co/sL9FeHv3UN

Shanthia Espinosa (right), daughter of Saipan, and her colleague, Gee Setthavongsack, visited the congressional office Washington while in town for the National Institutes of Health Science Education Conference (SciEd2023).

Thanks for visiting! https://t.co/WmJBgVG9Ff

.@cnmichcc will receive $1,700,000 to expand community partnerships and address health disparities, the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR) announced Thursday.

Congratulations, CHCC! https://t.co/T7A8Ez14yN

The House Appropriations Committee advanced two fiscal year 2024 funding bills last week containing funds for nine Marianas projects that I requested.

From more money for road improvements to wastewater treatment, see $6.9M worth of projects here:
https://t.co/u4SkCwTmbm https://t.co/EDDgw21dfF

Marianas veterans or their survivors now have until August 14, 2023 to file retroactive benefit claims under the PACT Act for a toxic exposure-related medical condition.

More info on the PACT Act & benefits eligibility can be found here:
https://t.co/yr8jgMfWDL https://t.co/xgSLrJkfyv

Of 87 NMI Veterans who applied for benefits under the PACT Act, 34 have been approved so far. Another 29 Vets are now enrolled with the .@DeptVetAffairs, as a result of the expanded coverage provided by the new law. https://t.co/z7LKUuutiy

Vets who deployed to a combat zone, never enrolled in VA healthcare, & left the military b/w 09/11/01 & 10/01/13 are eligible to enroll in VA healthcare directly w/out 1st applying for VA benefits.  Special enrollment ends Sept 30.  For more info, visit https://t.co/I73Sc2yyGj. https://t.co/No32uiINIQ

Seniors in the Marianas can look forward to lower drug prices for key medications, following last week’s announcement by the Biden administration of the first 10 drugs that will have their prices negotiated by the Medicare program.

Read more:
https://t.co/wskIEtS1H8 https://t.co/pYm2ovroHv
